who: Eliud Kipchoge · Vienna, 12 Oct 2019, after a marathon in 1:59:40 · BBC
quote: This shows no-one is limited. Now I've done it, I am expecting more people to do it after me.
meaning: When one person does it, the rest of us know it can be done.

who: John Landy and Roger Bannister · the mile, 1954
quote: John Landy ran the mile in 4:02 six times. Then, on 6 May 1954, Roger Bannister ran 3:59.4. Forty-six days later, Landy ran 3:58.0.
meaning: A wall looks solid until someone walks through it. Then others follow.

who: Seneca · Letters to Lucilius 6.5, tr. R. M. Gummere, 1917
quote: ...the way is long if one follows precepts, but short and helpful, if one follows patterns.
meaning: Rules make the road long. A living example makes it short.

who: Gertrude Ederle and her coach Bill Burgess · English Channel, 1926
quote: In 1925, Gertrude Ederle's first try to swim the English Channel was stopped. Then she trained with Bill Burgess, who swam it in 1911. In 1926 she crossed in under 15 hours.
meaning: Her coach had crossed that sea before. With him, she crossed it too.

who: Nainoa Thompson, student of navigator Mau Piailug · Polynesian Voyaging Society
quote: In 1976, Mau Piailug guided the canoe Hokule'a to Tahiti with no instruments. His student Nainoa said: ‘I watched what he watched.’ In 1980, Nainoa navigated it to Tahiti in 33 days.
meaning: He watched his teacher closely, then sailed the same long road.

who: Swami Vivekananda, on meeting his teacher Sri Ramakrishna · My Master, 1901
quote: ...when I myself saw this man, all scepticism was brushed aside. It could be done...
meaning: He met someone who had done it, and his doubt disappeared.

quote: ...there is a means of crossing this sea of relative existence; that very way by which sages have gone beyond it, I shall inculcate to thee.
meaning: Others have crossed this sea. I will show you the way they took.

quote: In 1488, at 13, Michelangelo was placed for three years with the painter Domenico Ghirlandaio, ‘in order to learn to paint.’
meaning: Even Michelangelo started as a boy learning from a master.

who: Isaac Newton · letter to Robert Hooke, February 1676
quote: If I have seen further it is by standing on the shoulders of Giants.
meaning: We see far because the people before us lift us up.

who: Japanese word origin · Daijisen; Nihon Kokugo Daijiten
quote: Manabu, ‘to learn’, shares its root with manebu. Old meanings of manebu: ‘to copy a model’ and ‘to take in what a teacher teaches.’
meaning: In Japanese, ‘to learn’ and ‘to copy’ grow from the same word.
